title: Vegetable Pulav
subtitle: One-pot pressure-cooker rice with tomato, capsicum and peas — best with kadhi or cold curd.
protein: ~7–8g protein per adult serving — from rice and peas

method.title: Temper and cook the pulav
items: Heat {@ghee:base} in a pressure cooker; add {@mustard} and {@cloves} and let them crackle
Add {@rice} and mix nicely; pour in {@water} — water should reach two finger-joints above the rice
Bring to a boil, then close the lid and cook 4–5 whistles; take off the flame and let the pressure drop on its own

method.label: Toddler — scoop hers here (before the spice tadka)
items: Fluff and spoon {=½ cup} of pulav into her bowl, picking out the cloves
Stir in {@carrot:toddler} and a dab of the serving ghee

method.title: Spice tadka for the adults
items: Heat {@ghee-tadka} in a small pan; add {@peppercorns} and {@green-chili}, then turn off the flame
Stir in {@chili-powder} and {@garam-masala} off the heat so they don't burn
Pour over the remaining pulav; fold through gently and sprinkle {@coriander}
Serve hot, topped with {@ghee:serve}, with kadhi or cold curd

method.label: Tip
method.text: The peppercorns, green chili, chili powder and garam masala used to go into the cooker; they now go in as a tadka after cooking, so her portion comes out mild and the adults get a brighter spice. Hing was added to the tempering. A stovetop pressure cooker or the Instant Pot (Pressure Cook high 6 min, natural release 10 min).
